headline: Law extends federal tax breaks for people with uninsured disaster losses and for people who receive wildfire relief payments.
what_it_does: People can deduct unreimbursed personal property losses from a federally declared major disaster if the loss is more than $500 per event, whether or not they itemize. This law covers disasters whose incident period begins between December 28, 2019, and the end of 2026, instead of ending in mid-2025. It also lets people leave wildfire relief payments out of their taxable income for federally declared forest or range fires from 2015 through 2026, no matter when the payment is received. It also adds legal authority for several related tax rules.

who_it_affects.group: People whose homes or personal property were damaged in federally declared major disasters
who_it_affects.how: They can deduct unreimbursed losses over $500 per disaster for disasters that begin through the end of 2026, even if they take the standard deduction.

who_it_affects.group: People who receive payments for wildfire damage
who_it_affects.how: They do not owe federal income tax on qualified relief payments tied to federally declared forest or range fires from 2015 through 2026, regardless of when the money arrives.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted September 11, 2026; covers disasters with incident periods beginning December 28, 2019, through December 31, 2026.
